  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 210,
      "endEvent": 211,
      "contextStartEvent": 181,
      "contextEndEvent": 222,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "skepticism is actually a metaphysical disease",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The quoted diagnosis could discredit skeptical objections by treating skepticism as a defect. However, Rhodes supplies a methodological argument about inferring wholes from parts (E181-E208, E215-E222) and disclaims a personal insult (E212-E214). It is unclear whether the diagnosis replaces that argument or makes disagreement itself disqualifying."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 407,
      "endEvent": 419,
      "contextStartEvent": 399,
      "contextEndEvent": 485,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "if they're advocating for positions that don't rise to the level of meeting the rigorous standards of skepticism",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Dillahunty suggests that criticism of skepticism or scientism comes from positions unable to meet their standards. This could preempt methodological criticism without assessing its merits. However, the wording is conditional, and he subsequently explains evidence assessment with an independently investigable receipt (E431-E485); no blanket rejection of criticism is explicit."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 819,
      "endEvent": 827,
      "contextStartEvent": 794,
      "contextEndEvent": 910,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "so to look for god by the scientific method is to commit a category mistake",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The category-mistake formula limits empirical inquiry, but Rhodes gives a reason: the proposed creator transcends the world's parameters (E812-E827), followed by an argument from participation in existence. Whether this excludes relevant contrary evidence is unclear; later he expressly considers historical miracles and prophecy as evidence (E2934-E2956)."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2197,
      "endEvent": 2201,
      "contextStartEvent": 2135,
      "contextEndEvent": 2205,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you cannot describe the whole by the part",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The formula ends a request for evidence after Dillahunty challenges the inference from parts to an agent (E2148-E2173). Earlier methodological reasoning supports a limited version (E181-E222), but its relevance to this specific inference is not established. It is unclear whether Rhodes protects the claim or reiterates his preferred evidential method."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2220,
      "endEvent": 2231,
      "contextStartEvent": 2211,
      "contextEndEvent": 2231,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "perfect unity and diversity within his very nature",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Asked how a partless God obtains data and creates complex life, Rhodes repeats unity grounding multiplicity and identifies the Christian God. The mechanism and specifically Christian inference remain unexplained here. However, E891-E910 already offers a unity-and-diversity argument for the Trinity, making this potentially an inadequate summary rather than substitution."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2255,
      "endEvent": 2257,
      "contextStartEvent": 2250,
      "contextEndEvent": 2257,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you can't give what you don't have",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The maxim supplies the entire answer to why God is conscious, without establishing that producing consciousness requires possessing consciousness. Rhodes later qualifies possession as causal capacity, illustrated by giving a black eye without having one (E2870-E2884). That clarification limits the maxim but does not earn the original inference to divine consciousness."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2774,
      "endEvent": 2783,
      "contextStartEvent": 2746,
      "contextEndEvent": 2786,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "miracles decline just as videotape starts climbing up",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Dillahunty turns an example of germ theory replacing spiritual explanations (E2769-E2773) into a general inverse relationship between investigation and divine manifestations. No evidence establishes the claimed decline with videotaping. His acknowledgement that he is preaching (E2785-E2786) marks the aside but does not supply the missing comparative evidence or immunize it."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3155,
      "endEvent": 3160,
      "contextStartEvent": 3145,
      "contextEndEvent": 3166,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "i couldn't give any empirical uh evidence",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Rhodes rejects empirical evidence when asked to justify the transition from a creator to Christianity and exclude alternatives. His whole-versus-part rationale does not explain why historical evidence would be irrelevant, especially given E2934-E2956. This may insulate the transition, but fatigue and his earlier openness to historical testing leave protective use uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3202,
      "endEvent": 3213,
      "contextStartEvent": 3167,
      "contextEndEvent": 3220,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "just because i projected a certain understanding on who he was doesn't mean that that's who he was",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Responding to what could change his belief, Rhodes describes suffering, felt divine presence, and revised expectations of God. Reclassifying disappointing expectations as projections could protect belief, but he never says every adverse result is irrelevant. He acknowledges suffering genuinely threatened his faith (E3178-E3201); this remains personal testimony rather than public proof."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 3042,
      "endEvent": 3106,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the time to be convinced of something is after there's sufficient evidence for it",
      "explanation": "The maxim is supported by examples of allocating research resources and agreed paranormal tests. Dillahunty explicitly distinguishes failed demonstrations from proof that dowsing is false (E3094-E3103), leaving room for new evidence."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2870,
      "endEvent": 2884,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "i don't have to have a black eye myself to give them a black eye",
      "explanation": "Rhodes qualifies his causal maxim with a concrete counterexample to literal possession. He explains that having an effect means having the ability to produce it; this informative qualification does not itself prove the earlier claim about divine consciousness."
    }
  ]
}
